Circle what you love — just like Grandma did.

Welcome in

The catalog we wished someone would mail us

Remember the big holiday catalog that landed on the porch with a thunk? You circled things in pen, folded down corners, and left it open on the coffee table as a hint. This is that book — except every single page is a real shop in Kokomo, most of them within a few blocks of each other downtown.

How to use it: tap the curled corner at the bottom of each page to turn it. Tap “Circle this wish ♡” on anything you love and it lands on your Wish List near the back.

The plan, in three steps

  1. 1 · This draft. Every shop below is presented as if it has already said yes — listings built from what each business actually sells or does, with real addresses. Prices are left “in store,” the way a good neighbor would.
  2. 2 · The invitation. Take this draft shop to shop. Each business picks its hero items, confirms hours, and chooses the gift ideas it wants circled most.
  3. 3 · The real edition. Photograph the actual shelves, print a short run for the holidays, and keep this digital book as the always-open copy.

A note on prices — Wish Books lived on prices, but this draft doesn't invent any. Every item says price in store until the shop itself sets it.

Art · Founded 1926 · 100 Years in 2026

Kokomo Art Association

📍 Artworks Gallery — 210 N. Main St.kaaonline.org ↗Art Center — 525 W. Ricketts St., Highland Park

A century of Kokomo making art together. The Association began in 1926 meeting in members' homes; today it runs the three-story Artworks Gallery downtown — which it owns — and the Kokomo Art Center in Highland Park, home of its permanent collection of Hoosier art. Admission to the Art Center is free.

Wish No. 801

An Original Work by a Kokomo Artist

Artworks Gallery is where working local artists sell their work — paintings, photography and more, across three floors. A gift with exactly one of it in the world.

One of a kind

Price in gallery

Wish No. 802

A Year of Membership

Join the hundred-year-old club: meetings, exhibits, competitions, classes — and free registration for the Annual Holiday Bazaar.

Centennial year

Price at kaaonline.org

Wish No. 803

The Annual Holiday Bazaar

November–December at Artworks Gallery: the season's handmade market, and the most Wish-Book event in Kokomo.

Nov–Dec

Price in gallery

Wish No. 804

Art Center Afternoon + Gift Shop

Rotating exhibits Tue–Sat 1–4 (Feb–Nov), the volunteer-run gift shop of small artful pieces, and the Little Free Art Library out front — take a piece, leave a piece, 24/7.

Art Glass · Since 1888

Kokomo Opalescent Glass

📍 1310 S. Market St.kog.com ↗Mon–Sat

The oldest art glass company in the United States has been making colored sheet glass in Kokomo since 1888 — glass that ends up in windows, lamps and art all over the world, made a mile from where you're standing.

First Friday Favorites · 5:30–8pm · After Hours 21+ After 8

The Best Night of the Month, Downtown

On the first Friday of every month, downtown Kokomo stays open late and fills up — shops host makers, galleries hang new work, and Courthouse Square turns into a market. Here's who's showing up, and what to circle:

First Friday

MoJoe Coffee House

📍 106 N. Main St. — Coffee, all-day breakfast, and a live-music host's welcome to start the night.


First Friday

Cook McDoogal's Irish Pub

📍 100 N. Main St. — Fish & Chips, Shepherd's Pie, the signature Reuben. Dinner first, wandering after.


First Friday

Secondhand Stories Books

📍 107 W. Mulberry St. — Used books, Blind Date with a Book, book-themed gifts, free coffee — and shop dog Dottie, accepting pets.


First Friday

Kokomo Antique Mall

📍 121 W. Sycamore St. — All three floors open until 8pm on First Fridays. Treasure-hunting after dark.


First Friday

Nailzx.jazz

📍 113 W. Sycamore St. — Create-your-own press-on nail sets: pick the shapes, pick the art, wear them home.


First Friday

The Anchor Hosts

Sound of Music (106 W. Walnut) · Fired Arts Studio (111 W. Sycamore) · Artworks Gallery / KAA (210 N. Main) · P.F. Hendricks (101 N. Buckeye) hosts StudioD13 and other makers in-store.

    PAGE 20

    Use the Whole Book in One Day

    The Saturday Downtown Loop

    1. 10am — Coffee & breakfast at MoJoe Coffee House, 106 N. Main.
    2. 11am — Art glass at Kokomo Opalescent Glass, 1310 S. Market (tour day!), then Artworks Gallery, 210 N. Main.
    3. 12pm — Geek Street: Kokomo Toys (111 E. Sycamore), AC TCG (126 W. Walnut), and a diamond-window stop at Palmer's (101 E. Sycamore).
    4. 1pm — Paint something at Fired Arts Studio, 111 W. Sycamore — pick it up next week.
    5. 2pm — Try on the town: The Elevated Hippie, Annmarie's, Olive Tree's charm bar, and P.F. Hendricks for the trail-to-table layer.
    6. 3pm — Strum something at Sound of Music, 106 W. Walnut. You have always wanted to.
    7. 4pm — Three floors of antiques at Kokomo Antique Mall, 121 W. Sycamore, and used-book luck at Secondhand Stories, 107 W. Mulberry — say hi to Dottie.
    8. Evening — Upstairs for a Coterie Burger (21+ dine-in; carry-out for the ride home).

    About this draft

    A concept draft of a Kokomo local-business Wish Book, written as if every shop has said yes. Listings are built from each business's real offerings and addresses as researched in October 2026; hours can change, and no prices are stated — each shop sets its own when the real edition is made. Cover and interior art are painted catalog-style illustrations created for this draft, not photographs of the shops. Sources: the businesses' own listings and sites, Greater Kokomo, and Visit Kokomo.
